title: TailLoR: Protecting Principal Components in Parameter-Efficient Continual Learning
abstract: Parameter-efficient finetuning methods based on spectral decomposition have enabled progress in Continual Learning. In this paper we introduce TailLoR, which utilizes the singular bases U and V of the pre-trained weights as a fixed reference frame to learn a low-rank update applied to the singular value matrix. A soft spectral penalty discourages updates aligned with dominant singular directions, reducing interference while routing fine-grained adaptation into the highly flexible, long-tail spectral coordinates.

significance.justification: The paper refines a known technique (spectral decomposition for parameter-efficient finetuning) by introducing a soft spectral penalty to protect principal components, offering a reproducible method for reducing catastrophic forgetting in continual learning.

novelty.justification: The method presents a substantial new variation by using singular bases as a fixed reference frame and applying a soft penalty to protect dominant singular directions, a distinct approach from prior low-rank adaptation techniques.

reproducibility.justification: The method is described clearly enough to reimplement, including the core algorithm of applying a low-rank update to the singular value matrix with a soft spectral penalty, though no mention of public code or artifacts is made in the provided text.

clarity.justification: The abstract is solidly written, clearly stating the problem (continual learning interference), the proposed solution (TailLoR with a soft spectral penalty), and the intended mechanism (routing adaptation into long-tail spectral coordinates).

topical_fit.justification: The paper is clearly in scope, addressing parameter-efficient finetuning and continual learning for pre-trained models, which are core practical concerns for engineers building and adapting LLM-based systems.
